pathway.title: UBS Group AG — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First, capital is the anchor of the view. At 31 December 2025 eligible CET1 capital of USD 71,262 million exceeded the Swiss requirement of USD 52,448 million by USD 18,814 million, and eligible going concern capital of USD 91,176 million exceeded its requirement of USD 73,955 million by USD 17,221 million (Documentary Fact; 20-F page:229). Gone concern loss-absorbing capacity of USD 96,130 million exceeded its requirement of USD 52,917 million by USD 43,213 million (same page). On the leverage basis the cushions are thinner: CET1 of 4.39% of the leverage ratio denominator against 3.50%, and going concern capital of 5.62% against 5.00%. The mechanism is that losses are absorbed by CET1 and additional tier 1 before subordinated and senior unsecured creditors, so these cushions are the first protection for debt holders (Analyst Interpretation).

Second, funding and liquidity reduce refinancing risk. Customer deposits were USD 788,367 million at 31 December 2025, about 49% of total assets of USD 1,617,427 million, and loans and advances to customers were about 83% of deposits. High-quality liquid assets averaged USD 331.6 billion in the fourth quarter of 2025 and the liquidity coverage ratio was 182.6% against a floor of 100%, with USD 51.8 billion of assets excluded from the group figure as restricted in subsidiaries. Debt issued at amortized cost and fair value due within 12 months was USD 113.7 billion on an undiscounted basis including interest, which is below high-quality liquid assets by a factor of about 2.9 (Analyst Interpretation; a simple comparison, not a regulatory measure). Management reports a liquidity coverage ratio of 179% and a net stable funding ratio of 115% for the third quarter of 2026 (Management Language, rounded, averaging basis not stated).

Third, earnings are recovering from a low base but remain market-sensitive. Operating profit before tax was USD 8,853 million in FY2025 against USD 6,821 million in FY2024, an increase of about 30%, and net interest income was only USD 7,747 million of USD 49,573 million total revenues, so about 84% of revenue is non-interest income from fees and trading (Documentary Fact; 20-F page:371 and page:409). The reported cost / income ratio was 81.1% in FY2025. Management says the underlying ratio was 68.7% in the third quarter of 2026 and targets below 70% at the 2026 exit (Management Language, not reconciled in the pack). Because fee and trading income move with markets, profit and capital generation are exposed to market conditions, which weakens earnings-based protection but is cushioned by the capital above (Analyst Interpretation).

Fourth, the Swiss capital package is the largest identified risk. The 20-F states the company estimates UBS AG would need additional CET1 of around USD 22bn if all measures were implemented as proposed, which would raise the group CET1 ratio to around 18.5% from its target of around 14%, with a phase-in starting in 2028 at the earliest (Documentary Fact; 20-F page:88 and page:89). Management calls the September 2026 Upper House outcome very concerning (Management Language). The mechanism, in management's words, is that the capital would be trapped against foreign subsidiary investments, so it cannot support distributions or growth. The implication for creditors is mixed: a higher requirement strengthens loss absorption, but it can also reduce shareholder returns and prompt structural change whose effect on creditors is not assessable from the pack (Insufficient Information).

Fifth, legacy exposures and resolution mechanics matter for the holding company's creditors. The 20-F describes a single point of entry resolution strategy at UBS Group AG involving write-down of equity, AT1 and tier 2 and conversion of senior unsecured bonds of UBS Group AG to equity if required, and records Credit Suisse AT1 litigation in which UBS Group AG is a party as successor (20-F page:84 and page:113). Provisions for litigation, regulatory and similar matters were USD 2,200 million and acquisition-related contingent liabilities USD 531 million at 31 December 2025, and management says an appeal decision on the AT1 case is not expected before the first quarter of 2027. These are mechanics, not outcomes: no claim amount is supplied.

Sixth, the integration is near completion, which should lower execution risk, but this is management's claim. Cumulative gross cost savings reached USD 13.2 billion by the third quarter of 2026 on management's figures, against USD 10.7 billion at the end of 2025, and Non-core and Legacy still reported a litigation charge of USD 275 million in the third quarter (Management Language; Q3 call).

runs.text: Strengths. A capital base well above requirements on all three Swiss measures (Documentary Fact), with management guiding to a CET1 ratio of around 14%. A deposit-led balance sheet with large high-quality liquid assets and a liquidity coverage ratio of 182.6% (Documentary Fact). A diversified revenue base across five divisions and four regions, with Switzerland at 32% of FY2025 revenue and the Americas at 36% (Documentary Fact). Earnings that improved in FY2025 and, on management's account, in 2026 (Documentary Fact and Management Language). No sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed, so sponsor extraction is not an evident risk (Analyst Interpretation; the evidence is an absence in a limited pack).

Weaknesses. Dependence on one regulator's rule change: the company estimate of around USD 22bn of extra CET1 at UBS AG is large against CET1 capital of USD 71,262 million for the group (Documentary Fact for the estimate, Analyst Interpretation for the scale). Unquantified legacy litigation and an acquired-risk tail (Documentary Fact). Earnings that depend on fees and trading, with a reported cost / income ratio of 81.1% in FY2025 (Documentary Fact). Management plans to release the integration capital buffer from 2027 and continue buybacks, with USD 4.8 billion repurchased in 2026 to the third quarter and USD 1.2 billion more intended, and says it can build capital later from earnings (Management Language). The group's holding-company debt sits in the resolution path described above; terms by instrument are Not supplied (Insufficient Information).

Thesis. UBS Group AG's high capital and liquidity buffers support a strong credit view today, and the unresolved Swiss capital rules and legacy litigation, not near-term liquidity or debt service, are what could weaken it.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The defining transaction in the pack is the acquisition of Credit Suisse Group AG on 12 June 2023, after which UBS Group AG "succeeding by operation of Swiss law to all assets and liabilities of Credit Suisse Group AG" (20-F page:41). The 20-F states the acquisition followed a request from the Swiss Federal Department of Finance, the Swiss National Bank and FINMA (page:40). The consideration included UBS Group AG shares (treasury shares transferred, page:377) and the 20-F records negative goodwill of 27,264 USD m in FY2023 (page:371); no purchase agreement or term sheet is supplied, so deal terms beyond these statements are Not supplied. Integration is described as substantially complete at the end of 2026: UBS AG and Credit Suisse AG merged in May 2024, UBS Switzerland AG and Credit Suisse (Schweiz) AG in July 2024, and further US and EU entity mergers followed in 2025 (page:41). Management says all former Credit Suisse client migrations were complete in March 2026 (Q1 call page:3). Creditor mechanics: a simpler legal structure and decommissioned legacy systems reduce operational and resolution complexity, while the remaining Non-core and Legacy book and acquired litigation keep a tail of loss and cash-cost risk until wound down. The year-end 2026 completion claim is management language and not yet evidenced by a filed statement.

Disposals and exits around the transaction: the sale of Select Portfolio Servicing was completed in March 2025 with a gain of 97 USD m and a reduction of about USD 1.3bn in risk-weighted assets (20-F page:42); the 50% interest in Swisscard was sold to American Express with completion in January 2026, a subsequent event relative to the FY2025 period, with a gain expected in the first quarter of 2026 (page:42); the Q1 call attributes a limited tax charge to that gain (page:5); and the sale of O'Connor was completed in the first quarter of 2026 (Q1 call page:8, and "the O'Connor exit" in Q3 call page:8). Prices for these disposals are not given except where stated. Management also reports the conversion of UBS Bank USA to a national bank charter (Q1 call page:3) with product roll-out expected in 2027 (Q3 call page:12).

New debt issues and liability management: the pack does not list any individual new bond, with coupon, maturity, size or issuer; that detail is Not supplied. What it does show is (i) 2025 cash flows from issuance of debt designated at fair value and long-term debt at amortized cost of 131,476 USD m against repayments of 154,614 USD m (20-F page:379); (ii) in 2025, new issuances of AT1 capital instruments of USD 5.8 bn and a call of USD 3.2 bn equivalent of AT1 capital instruments, with loss-absorbing AT1 capital up by USD 3.5 bn to USD 19.9 bn (page:232); (iii) management's statement that the 2026 AT1 issuance plan was completed by mid-February 2026 (Q1 call page:6) and that further AT1 was pre-funded in the second quarter of 2026 (Q2 call page:5); (iv) total debt issued of 343,922 USD m at 31.3.26, 343,551 USD m at 30.6.26 and 324,981 USD m at 30.9.26; and (v) a third-quarter 2026 liability management transaction, "the repurchase of around 10 billion of high-cost Credit Suisse liabilities", which produced a charge of 346 million (Q3 call page:4). The sources do not say which instruments were repurchased, at what price, whether by tender or in the market, or whether holders were treated pro rata, so creditor treatment of that action is Insufficient Information and no conclusion is drawn on it. Management links it to lower funding drag in Non-core and Legacy and support for net interest income, which is its characterisation.

Capital returns act as a use of funds. The 20-F shows share repurchase programmes of USD 2,000 m each in 2024 and 2025 (page:377), an accrual of 3,449 USD m for the proposed 2025 dividend and a capital reserve of 3,000 USD m for expected 2026 repurchases (page:231). In 2026 management reports a USD 3 billion programme completed by the second quarter results, a further USD 3 billion programme to run to the end of the second quarter of 2027, 4.8 billion repurchased and 2.8 billion of dividend accrued year to date at Q3, and 1.2 billion more intended over the next three months (Q2 call page:3; Q3 call page:3). Management links the pace to maintaining a CET1 ratio of around 14% and to the Swiss Parliament's deliberations (Q2 call page:3). These are distributions funded from reported earnings and are conditioned on a stated capital ratio. The capital-return plan for 2027 is to be given with fourth quarter results (Q3 call page:3).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The pack describes a listed bank holding company whose main creditor-relevant change is the 2023 acquisition of Credit Suisse Group AG and the integration that management says will be substantially complete at the end of 2026. The group runs five divisions, of which Global Wealth Management and the Investment Bank carry most divisional profit, and non-interest income is the larger part of revenue. No sponsor or controlling owner is disclosed, and the only holders above 3% named in the 20-F are Norges Bank and BlackRock Inc., so sponsor-behaviour analysis reduces to documented capital-return conduct. The transaction set for 2025 and 2026 consists of disposals, entity mergers, capital instruments and a liability management action in the third quarter of 2026, for which the pack gives amounts and charges but no instrument terms. The Swiss capital proposals and the legacy litigation are the main credit uncertainties and are described but not quantified by any rule text or court document in the pack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The defining transaction in the pack is the acquisition of Credit Suisse Group AG on 12 June 2023, after which UBS Group AG "succeeding by operation of Swiss law to all assets and liabilities of Credit Suisse Group AG" (20-F page:41). The 20-F states the acquisition followed a request from the Swiss Federal Department of Finance, the Swiss National Bank and FINMA (page:40). The consideration included UBS Group AG shares (treasury shares transferred, page:377) and the 20-F records negative goodwill of 27,264 USD m in FY2023 (page:371); no purchase agreement or term sheet is supplied, so deal terms beyond these statements are Not supplied. Integration is described as substantially complete at the end of 2026: UBS AG and Credit Suisse AG merged in May 2024, UBS Switzerland AG and Credit Suisse (Schweiz) AG in July 2024, and further US and EU entity mergers followed in 2025 (page:41). Management says all former Credit Suisse client migrations were complete in March 2026 (Q1 call page:3). Creditor mechanics: a simpler legal structure and decommissioned legacy systems reduce operational and resolution complexity, while the remaining Non-core and Legacy book and acquired litigation keep a tail of loss and cash-cost risk until wound down. The year-end 2026 completion claim is management language and not yet evidenced by a filed statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disposals and exits around the transaction: the sale of Select Portfolio Servicing was completed in March 2025 with a gain of 97 USD m and a reduction of about USD 1.3bn in risk-weighted assets (20-F page:42); the 50% interest in Swisscard was sold to American Express with completion in January 2026, a subsequent event relative to the FY2025 period, with a gain expected in the first quarter of 2026 (page:42); the Q1 call attributes a limited tax charge to that gain (page:5); and the sale of O'Connor was completed in the first quarter of 2026 (Q1 call page:8, and "the O'Connor exit" in Q3 call page:8). Prices for these disposals are not given except where stated. Management also reports the conversion of UBS Bank USA to a national bank charter (Q1 call page:3) with product roll-out expected in 2027 (Q3 call page:12).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt issues and liability management: the pack does not list any individual new bond, with coupon, maturity, size or issuer; that detail is Not supplied. What it does show is (i) 2025 cash flows from issuance of debt designated at fair value and long-term debt at amortized cost of 131,476 USD m against repayments of 154,614 USD m (20-F page:379); (ii) in 2025, new issuances of AT1 capital instruments of USD 5.8 bn and a call of USD 3.2 bn equivalent of AT1 capital instruments, with loss-absorbing AT1 capital up by USD 3.5 bn to USD 19.9 bn (page:232); (iii) management's statement that the 2026 AT1 issuance plan was completed by mid-February 2026 (Q1 call page:6) and that further AT1 was pre-funded in the second quarter of 2026 (Q2 call page:5); (iv) total debt issued of 343,922 USD m at 31.3.26, 343,551 USD m at 30.6.26 and 324,981 USD m at 30.9.26; and (v) a third-quarter 2026 liability management transaction, "the repurchase of around 10 billion of high-cost Credit Suisse liabilities", which produced a charge of 346 million (Q3 call page:4). The sources do not say which instruments were repurchased, at what price, whether by tender or in the market, or whether holders were treated pro rata, so creditor treatment of that action is Insufficient Information and no conclusion is drawn on it. Management links it to lower funding drag in Non-core and Legacy and support for net interest income, which is its characterisation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital returns act as a use of funds. The 20-F shows share repurchase programmes of USD 2,000 m each in 2024 and 2025 (page:377), an accrual of 3,449 USD m for the proposed 2025 dividend and a capital reserve of 3,000 USD m for expected 2026 repurchases (page:231). In 2026 management reports a USD 3 billion programme completed by the second quarter results, a further USD 3 billion programme to run to the end of the second quarter of 2027, 4.8 billion repurchased and 2.8 billion of dividend accrued year to date at Q3, and 1.2 billion more intended over the next three months (Q2 call page:3; Q3 call page:3). Management links the pace to maintaining a CET1 ratio of around 14% and to the Swiss Parliament's deliberations (Q2 call page:3). These are distributions funded from reported earnings and are conditioned on a stated capital ratio. The capital-return plan for 2027 is to be given with fourth quarter results (Q3 call page:3).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 20-F states that proposed legislation would require deduction of investments in foreign subsidiaries of systemically important banks from CET1 capital, entering into force in 2028 at the earliest, with a 65% deduction in the first year rising by 5-percentage-point steps to 100% (page:88).

fields.name: Quote

This is a description of the stated strategy, not a legal interpretation of creditor ranking.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Credit Suisse AT1 litigation: cases lodged against FINMA over the AT1 write-down, with UBS Group AG a party as successor (20-F page:113); management says no decision is expected before the first quarter of 2027 (Q3 call page:14). Provisions are in the financial base handoff; no claim amount is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue durability. Evidence: net interest income is 7,747 USD m of 49,573 USD m total revenues and Global Wealth Management earns recurring net fee income on fee-generating assets (20-F pages:409 and 49 to 50). Mechanic: revenue depends on market levels, client activity and asset flows more than on loan margins, so revenue moves with markets. Implication: debt service capacity for a group of this size rests on earnings volatility and capital buffers, not on contractual interest cover; the financial base handoff gives the capital and liquidity figures. A logged conflict that counters part of this: none on revenue; the headcount measure conflict only affects cost-per-head analysis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Margin and cash flow risk. Evidence: operating expenses of 40,197 USD m and a reported cost / income ratio of 81.1% for FY2025, with management targeting below 70% underlying by year-end 2026 (20-F pages:371, 37, 47). Mechanic: integration cost savings are the planned margin driver, but they require integration expenses (Q3 call page:5). Implication: the margin path depends on completing the integration; the target is management language and the cost-to-achieve conflict above limits how far the savings economics can be checked.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Concentration risk. Evidence: Switzerland provides 32% of revenue and 49% of non-current assets, and the wealth and bank divisions carry most divisional profit (20-F pages:410, 409). Mechanic: Swiss regulation, the Swiss economy and the Swiss capital rules touch both the largest region and the group's legal structure. Implication: a Swiss rule change has outsized effect on distributions and structure; the company's own estimate of around USD 22bn extra CET1 at the bank subsidiary is the size marker.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Sponsor alignment. Evidence: no sponsor or controlling holder disclosed (20-F page:262) and capital returns tied to a ratio target. Mechanic: there is no sponsor incentive for debt-funded extraction, but shareholder distributions compete with capital builds. Implication: monitor distribution decisions against the Swiss rule outcome; no extraction behaviour is evidenced and no conclusion on willingness is drawn.

fields.value: Issuer sources relied on (pinned `.jsonl` text; locators are `page:N` extraction chunks). The credit view rests on the upstream handoffs below; the issuer sources were opened to check the capital requirements, the Swiss proposals and the funding notes cited in this handoff.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: UBS Group AG is, on the evidence supplied, a strong and well-capitalized bank credit whose main risks are regulatory and legacy rather than earnings or liquidity. The strongest support is capital and liquidity: at 31 December 2025 CET1 capital was USD 71,262 million, 14.44% of risk-weighted assets against a Swiss requirement of 10.63%; the liquidity coverage ratio averaged 182.6% in the fourth quarter of 2025; and management reports a CET1 ratio of 14.7% at 30 September 2026. The weakest point is the Swiss capital package, which the company estimates would need around USD 22bn of extra CET1 at UBS AG, alongside unquantified Credit Suisse litigation. The outcome turns on the final Swiss rules and on how management balances buybacks against capital building.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, capital is the anchor of the view. At 31 December 2025 eligible CET1 capital of USD 71,262 million exceeded the Swiss requirement of USD 52,448 million by USD 18,814 million, and eligible going concern capital of USD 91,176 million exceeded its requirement of USD 73,955 million by USD 17,221 million (Documentary Fact; 20-F page:229). Gone concern loss-absorbing capacity of USD 96,130 million exceeded its requirement of USD 52,917 million by USD 43,213 million (same page). On the leverage basis the cushions are thinner: CET1 of 4.39% of the leverage ratio denominator against 3.50%, and going concern capital of 5.62% against 5.00%. The mechanism is that losses are absorbed by CET1 and additional tier 1 before subordinated and senior unsecured creditors, so these cushions are the first protection for debt holders (Analyst Interpretation).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, funding and liquidity reduce refinancing risk. Customer deposits were USD 788,367 million at 31 December 2025, about 49% of total assets of USD 1,617,427 million, and loans and advances to customers were about 83% of deposits. High-quality liquid assets averaged USD 331.6 billion in the fourth quarter of 2025 and the liquidity coverage ratio was 182.6% against a floor of 100%, with USD 51.8 billion of assets excluded from the group figure as restricted in subsidiaries. Debt issued at amortized cost and fair value due within 12 months was USD 113.7 billion on an undiscounted basis including interest, which is below high-quality liquid assets by a factor of about 2.9 (Analyst Interpretation; a simple comparison, not a regulatory measure). Management reports a liquidity coverage ratio of 179% and a net stable funding ratio of 115% for the third quarter of 2026 (Management Language, rounded, averaging basis not stated).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, earnings are recovering from a low base but remain market-sensitive. Operating profit before tax was USD 8,853 million in FY2025 against USD 6,821 million in FY2024, an increase of about 30%, and net interest income was only USD 7,747 million of USD 49,573 million total revenues, so about 84% of revenue is non-interest income from fees and trading (Documentary Fact; 20-F page:371 and page:409). The reported cost / income ratio was 81.1% in FY2025. Management says the underlying ratio was 68.7% in the third quarter of 2026 and targets below 70% at the 2026 exit (Management Language, not reconciled in the pack). Because fee and trading income move with markets, profit and capital generation are exposed to market conditions, which weakens earnings-based protection but is cushioned by the capital above (Analyst Interpretation).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, the Swiss capital package is the largest identified risk. The 20-F states the company estimates UBS AG would need additional CET1 of around USD 22bn if all measures were implemented as proposed, which would raise the group CET1 ratio to around 18.5% from its target of around 14%, with a phase-in starting in 2028 at the earliest (Documentary Fact; 20-F page:88 and page:89). Management calls the September 2026 Upper House outcome very concerning (Management Language). The mechanism, in management's words, is that the capital would be trapped against foreign subsidiary investments, so it cannot support distributions or growth. The implication for creditors is mixed: a higher requirement strengthens loss absorption, but it can also reduce shareholder returns and prompt structural change whose effect on creditors is not assessable from the pack (Insufficient Information).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth, legacy exposures and resolution mechanics matter for the holding company's creditors. The 20-F describes a single point of entry resolution strategy at UBS Group AG involving write-down of equity, AT1 and tier 2 and conversion of senior unsecured bonds of UBS Group AG to equity if required, and records Credit Suisse AT1 litigation in which UBS Group AG is a party as successor (20-F page:84 and page:113). Provisions for litigation, regulatory and similar matters were USD 2,200 million and acquisition-related contingent liabilities USD 531 million at 31 December 2025, and management says an appeal decision on the AT1 case is not expected before the first quarter of 2027. These are mechanics, not outcomes: no claim amount is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sixth, the integration is near completion, which should lower execution risk, but this is management's claim. Cumulative gross cost savings reached USD 13.2 billion by the third quarter of 2026 on management's figures, against USD 10.7 billion at the end of 2025, and Non-core and Legacy still reported a litigation charge of USD 275 million in the third quarter (Management Language; Q3 call).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. A capital base well above requirements on all three Swiss measures (Documentary Fact), with management guiding to a CET1 ratio of around 14%. A deposit-led balance sheet with large high-quality liquid assets and a liquidity coverage ratio of 182.6% (Documentary Fact). A diversified revenue base across five divisions and four regions, with Switzerland at 32% of FY2025 revenue and the Americas at 36% (Documentary Fact). Earnings that improved in FY2025 and, on management's account, in 2026 (Documentary Fact and Management Language). No sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed, so sponsor extraction is not an evident risk (Analyst Interpretation; the evidence is an absence in a limited pack).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Dependence on one regulator's rule change: the company estimate of around USD 22bn of extra CET1 at UBS AG is large against CET1 capital of USD 71,262 million for the group (Documentary Fact for the estimate, Analyst Interpretation for the scale). Unquantified legacy litigation and an acquired-risk tail (Documentary Fact). Earnings that depend on fees and trading, with a reported cost / income ratio of 81.1% in FY2025 (Documentary Fact).
